questions.prompt: When is a BARE (unquoted) expansion the right call?

options.a: whenever the value contains no spaces
options.c: when you deliberately want the shell to split or glob the result — e.g. a variable holding a glob pattern that should match files; rare, and it should look intentional

questions.prompt: Inside "'$user'" (double quotes outermost), what do the single quotes do?

options.a: they block the expansion — the argument is literally $user
options.b: nothing special — they are ordinary characters there, and $user still expands
options.c: it is a syntax error: quotes cannot appear inside quotes

questions.prompt: (L1.7 preview) Does "$(hostname)" still run hostname inside double quotes?

options.a: yes — command substitution expands inside double quotes; the quotes only stop splitting/globbing of its output
options.b: no — double quotes make it literal text
options.c: only when the shell is interactive
